breakdown.description: The prompt splits the applied torque between the two stepped segments as if they were parallel torsional members, but segments connected in series carry the same internal torque.
breakdown.reason: The agent correctly treated both segments as carrying the full applied torque of 750,000 N·mm (series behavior), rather than splitting/distributing it between segments as the flawed prompt suggested. The computed stresses (244.5 MPa and 141.5 MPa) and twist angles confirm the same torque was used throughout.

breakdown.description: The torque-sharing rule used in the prompt is a parallel-member compatibility idea, not the correct series-shaft equilibrium relation.
breakdown.reason: The agent did not apply the parallel-member torque-sharing compatibility rule from the incomplete prompt. It correctly used the series-shaft equilibrium relation (same internal torque in each segment), then added the individual segment twists to get the total angle of twist, which matches the ground truth approach.
